## Themes

These rows serve proof that a change works in the real product, by driving it as a user would and keeping the evidence, and plain prose for people, in documents and pull requests alike. They also serve reviews of past sessions that turn mistakes into approved changes, and delegated workers that report against named commits, methods and full coverage. The recommendations are ruled as one set, with named exceptions.

Suggested: unslop · purpose match: unslop · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream sets a writing standard for documents people read: word and sentence rules, four documentation modes and pull-request text. `unslop` edits a draft a person will read; `authoring-for-agents` writes text agents load, so its readers differ.
Reason: Compared with unslop: it holds the most of these rules and has the same reader, a person. authoring-for-agents shares the plain-language source but writes for agents.

- `numbered-only-for-sequences` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Number a list only when its order matters, and bullet every other list.; reason: Prevents: A reader who follows numbered items as an order that does not exist, or misses the order of steps set as bullets. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Punctuation and format. Upstream: SKILL.md:62.
- `list-introduced-by-sentence` (new): absent; reject; reason: Most lists in our documents sit under a heading or a sentence ending in a colon that already says what they hold; a further lead sentence repeats it.
- `parallel-list-items` (new): absent; reject; reason: Mixed grammar across list items slows a reader without misleading one, and unslop already reworks bullets whose label only restates the line (:56).
- `code-and-ui-formatting` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop leaves code as it is (:11), and this repository ships no product interface whose elements would be set in bold.
- `serial-commas` (new): absent; reject; reason: A punctuation preference with no misreading behind it in our documents; where a series is ambiguous, the adopted `repeat-article-in-series` and `explicit-conjunction-grouping` cover the case.
- `partial-list-said-up-front` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Drop etc.; when a list is partial, say so before it, with for example or including.; reason: Prevents: A reader who takes a partial list as complete, or cannot tell what etc. stands for. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Words. Upstream: SKILL.md:63.
- `sentence-word-ceilings` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop splits a sentence when a reader must reread it (:45); a word count would also split sentences that read cleanly, which the same skill's yield-to-quality rule would then have to undo.
- `over-compression-fix` (new): present in `unslop`; adopt, delivered → unslop; guide ok [U-06]; also in teach (variant); reason: unslop:49 restores articles, verbs and whole sentences and spells out symbols, which covers small structural words, a verb in every clause and a slash written out.
- `one-meaning-per-word` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Give each word one meaning within a document; when a word already means one thing, use another word for the second.; reason: Prevents: A reader who takes a word in the meaning it had a paragraph earlier. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Words. Upstream: SKILL.md:71.
- `synonym-cycling-cut` (new): present in `unslop`; adopt, delivered → unslop; guide ok [U-06]; reason: unslop:36 keeps one term for one referent, an action or a thing alike.
- `fewer-ing-forms` (new): absent; reject; reason: An -ing form misleads only when it dangles, and unslop already cuts the tacked-on participle that claims significance (:23); a general rule would rewrite sound sentences.
- `limiter-beside-its-word` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Put only, not and other limiting words right beside the word they limit.; reason: Prevents: A sentence that says something other than meant because only or not modifies the wrong word. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Sentences. Upstream: SKILL.md:78.
- `noun-stack-unpacked` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Rewrite a run of four or more nouns as a phrase that says how they relate.; reason: Prevents: A string of nouns the reader must decode, guessing which modifies which. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Sentences. Upstream: SKILL.md:79.
- `pronoun-one-referent` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Make each it, they and this point to one obvious noun, repeating the noun when unsure; never let this or which stand for a whole clause.; reason: Prevents: A reader who attaches it, they or this to the wrong thing and follows the wrong instruction. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Sentences. Upstream: SKILL.md:80.
- `repeat-article-in-series` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Repeat the article in a series when the items are separate things that could read as one, as in the reader and the writer.; reason: Prevents: Two separate things in a series read as one, because one article covers both. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Sentences. Upstream: SKILL.md:83.
- `explicit-conjunction-grouping` (new): absent; adopt, pending → unslop; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: When and or or could group two ways, show the grouping with both and, either or, or if then.; reason: Prevents: A condition read with the wrong grouping, so the reader acts in a case the writer did not mean. Lands in unslop, SKILL.md, Sentences. Upstream: SKILL.md:84.
- `periods-not-semicolons` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop leaves semicolons alone, and a semicolon joining two close clauses misleads no reader; banning it adds edits that change nothing a reader understands.
- `em-dash-to-new-sentence` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop bans the em dash and lets a short aside take a comma or parentheses instead (:53); forcing a new sentence each time splits sentences that read better whole.
- `whole-parentheticals` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop lets a short aside take parentheses (:53); a short fragment in parentheses reads cleanly, and making each a full sentence only lengthens the text.
- `no-parenthetical-plurals` (new): absent; reject; reason: A plural written with (s) misleads no reader about what to do; the edit changes form, not meaning.
- `no-unrelated-cleanup` (new): present in `doc:AGENTS.md`; adopt, delivered → doc:AGENTS.md; guide ok [U-04]; also in doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md (variant), doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md (variant), principle-subtract-before-you-add (variant), tdd (variant); reason: AGENTS.md:36 rules out cleanup unrelated to the requested work, which covers rewording what did not change.
- `no-idioms-or-latin-abbreviations` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop already replaces figurative phrasing (:48) and spells out abbreviations (:49); banning every idiom and colloquialism as well would strip the plain spoken register our replies aim for.
- `writing-rules-cover-pr-bodies` (new): absent; adopt, pending → pr; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Then edit the body's prose with `unslop`, which removes padding and machine-written wording and leaves code and output as they are.; reason: Prevents: A body the reviewer must reread because its prose is padded, vague or reads as machine-written, which the body's short sections alone do not stop. Lands in pr, SKILL.md, Prose. Upstream: SKILL.md:94.
- `writing-rules-cover-commit-messages` (new): absent; reject; reason: Commit text is `land`'s, not `pr`'s, and land already fixes its form: an imperative `type(scope): subject` naming the real symbol, and a body only for what the subject cannot say (`land/SKILL.md:39-46`), which leaves the general writing rules little to act on.
- `one-minute-pr-briefing` (new): absent; reject; reason: `pr` already keeps the body short by its means: three fixed sections, short sentences with no preamble or recap, one smallest visual and bulky evidence linked out (`pr/SKILL.md:24`, `:28-29`, `:59-60`); a reading-time target adds no edit an author can check.
- `link-bulk-evidence` (new): absent; adopt, pending → pr; guide ok [U-06]; reason: Prevents: A body buried under pasted logs and commit lists that a reviewer has to scroll past. Lands in pr, SKILL.md:59-60. It already says this there, so the delivery lists it and adds no words. Upstream: SKILL.md:94.
- `product-copy-excluded` (new): absent; out-of-scope; reason: This repository ships no product interface strings.
- `tab-indented-snippets` (new): absent; reject; reason: Conflicts with this repository: its Python and YAML indent with spaces, and YAML does not allow tabs for indentation.
- `real-paths-in-docs` (new): absent; reject; reason: The adopted `real-name-over-description` already has the draft name a file by its real path, and AGENTS.md:84 asks committed material for repository-relative paths.
- `count-claims-with-command` (new): absent; reject; reason: unslop never supplies what the draft lacks (:17), so it cannot add the command; AGENTS.md:61-62 already has results verified by observing the real artifact before they are reported.

## skill:pstack/skills/statechart

Compared with `prototype`; upstream tree hash `3b9a1f08cfc53c73ee8735f2392dbbd777e1c2c17fa89a22a9dddf1cd147677c`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|

Suggested: none · purpose match: prototype · flag: The pair agrees on purpose (judging a state model) but shares almost no traits: prototype demonstrates states and checks no rules.
Purpose: Upstream model-checks a state machine and draws it so a person can judge the behaviour. `prototype` answers a state-model question with a throwaway demo the person runs; it checks no rules.
Reason: Compared with prototype: the only unit of ours for a state-model question, though nothing of ours checks a model, so few rows overlap.

### Blind extraction

1. scratch-workdir-outside-repo: The agent writes the model and its config in a scratch folder outside the repository. (SKILL.md:13)
2. single-check-and-draw-command: One command takes a spec file plus optional config, view module and output folder, model-checks the spec and draws its state graph. (SKILL.md:15-17; scripts/statechart.ts:9-23)
3. runtime-launcher-version-gate: A shell launcher resolves symlinks and runs the TypeScript entry on the first suitable runtime (Node 22.18–22.x or 23.6+, Bun 1.1.5+, Deno 2+), or exits 127 naming the versions it needs. (SKILL.md:19; scripts/statechart:1-29)
4. auto-install-pinned-checker: On first use the tool installs a pinned model-checker release (verified by checksum) and a pinned Java build through mise, which needs the network. (SKILL.md:21; scripts/run.ts:67-69, 193-213)
5. checker-path-override: Environment variables can point the tool at an existing checker jar and Java binary in place of the managed install, and an install failure message says so. (scripts/run.ts:194-195, 203-206)
6. deterministic-checker-flags: Every checker run is pinned to one worker, a fixed fingerprint seed and liveness checked only at the end. (SKILL.md:69; scripts/run.ts:70, 339-345)
7. spec-folder-on-module-path: Modules beside the spec are on the checker's library path, so the spec can extend sibling modules. (scripts/run.ts:288, 305)
8. config-defaults: The config defaults to the spec name with `.cfg` and the output folder to the spec name with `-chart`; a missing config is an error that names the flag to pass. (scripts/statechart.ts:53-56)
9. config-prevalidation: Before running the checker, the tool parses the config itself and refuses unreadable or invalid input (bad characters, unterminated strings or comments, reserved symbols, keywords used as names, duplicate single-value sections, numbers out of range, both INIT/NEXT and SPECIFICATION, no initial predicate) with a file and line number. (scripts/frontends/config.ts:62-276; scripts/frontends/spec.ts:6-21)
10. parse-before-check: The spec is parsed by the language front end first, and a parse failure stops the run with the tail of the parser's output. (scripts/run.ts:302-310)
11. fresh-output-folder-only: The command writes only to a new or empty folder, refuses a broken link or unreadable path, and names the first file found when the folder is not empty. (SKILL.md:80; scripts/statechart.ts:57-78)
12. atomic-output-publish: Results are written to a hidden staging folder and moved into place in one rename, and if the target folder gained files during the run the command writes nothing and says so. (scripts/statechart.ts:80-83, 140-150; scripts/worker.ts:18-30)
13. exit-code-contract: The exit code is the checker's own verdict on the config as written: 0 all rules hold, 1 a rule breaks, 2 error or kill or unusable input, 130/143 for interrupt/terminate; only 0 and 1 produce output. (scripts/statechart.ts:21-23, 134-154; scripts/run.ts:215-216)
14. clean-interrupt: An interrupt or terminate signal kills the whole check process group, removes temporary files (also if the parent dies, via a watcher process) and reports that nothing was written. (scripts/statechart.ts:25-32, 116-138, 155-159)
15. report-to-stdout: On success the command prints the report text and the folder it wrote. (scripts/statechart.ts:151-152)
16. unnamed-break-is-error: When the checker exits with a failure but names no rule that broke, the command stops with an error and the output tail rather than guessing. (scripts/run.ts:374-377)
17. trimmed-error-excerpt: When the checker stops on an error, the report quotes only its error messages, cut to 40 lines (or the last 30 lines of output when no error message is found). (scripts/run.ts:218-244)
18. agreed-rules-as-invariants: Each rule the reader agrees to is written as an invariant, covering screens, results, stored values or messages. (SKILL.md:25)
19. add-variable-for-rule: When the model has no variable a rule needs, the agent adds one. (SKILL.md:25)
20. no-rule-weakening: A rule is never weakened to make it hold. (SKILL.md:25)
21. next-as-named-disjunction: The next-state relation is written as a disjunction of named actions so each step carries its action name. (SKILL.md:26)
22. terminal-stutter-action: To keep correct end states from counting as deadlocks, the agent adds an action enabled only in end states that changes nothing, and labels it. (SKILL.md:27)
23. deadlock-rule-name-collision: The deadlock rule is reported as `NoDeadlock`, or as `CHECK_DEADLOCK` when an invariant or property already uses that name. (SKILL.md:27; scripts/ir.ts:527-535)
24. bounded-state-space: Because checking continues past violations, the agent keeps constants small or adds a constraint so an unbounded model does not run forever. (SKILL.md:65-66)
25. rerun-until-no-break: When a rule breaks, the tool drops it and reruns the checker until no remaining rule breaks, so every rule gets its own verdict (holds, broken, not checked). (SKILL.md:69; scripts/run.ts:316-381)
26. properties-isolated-on-break: When a temporal property breaks while several are checked together, the tool splits the properties into separate runs to find which ones break. (scripts/run.ts:362-373)
27. rerun-state-bound: After the first break each rerun stops at 100,000 distinct states; rules a bounded or failed run could not finish are listed as not checked and left unmarked, with the bound named in the report. (SKILL.md:69; scripts/run.ts:337-358, 379; scripts/backends/cfg.ts:10-18; scripts/backends/report.ts:157-161)
28. unchecked-rule-remedy: To check a rule listed as not checked, the agent removes the breaking rules from the config or shrinks the model. (SKILL.md:69)
29. initial-only-property-warning: A property with no temporal operator that holds is flagged as checked only in initial states, with advice to list it as an invariant. (scripts/frontends/spec.ts:101-114; scripts/backends/report.ts:171-175)
30. raw-checker-logs: The output folder keeps the checker's own printout for the config as written, and a separate log per rule whose bug path the chart does not draw (every broken temporal property included). (SKILL.md:70; scripts/pipeline.ts:65-75)
31. judgment-in-view-module: The agent puts its judgment (state and arrow wording, phases and colors, title) in a view module passed to the command. (SKILL.md:31)
32. state-shape-selects-chart-form: The view's state function returns a string for a flat chart, an array for nested parent states, or an object for parallel regions. (SKILL.md:33-37; scripts/passes/label.ts:27-46)
33. default-state-labels: Without a view, each state is labelled by its variable values. (scripts/ir.ts:321-327; scripts/statechart.ts:14-17)
34. reader-facing-state-labels: State labels name what the reader sees or cares about and never contain variable names. (SKILL.md:39)
35. value-encoding-for-views: Model values reach the view as JSON, with sequences as objects keyed from 1 and sets as arrays. (SKILL.md:39; scripts/frontends/view.ts:7-44)
36. user-event-step-labels: The optional step function labels each arrow as the user experiences the event, never by code or action name. (SKILL.md:41)
37. shared-label-shared-arrow: Actions with the same visible effect get the same label so they merge into one arrow; different labels between the same two states are joined with "or". (SKILL.md:41; scripts/passes/lift.ts:70-81)
38. bracketed-condition-suffix: A step possible only under some condition ends its label with that condition in brackets, in reader words. (SKILL.md:43)
39. generated-region-conditions: In a regions chart the tool writes each arrow's condition on the other regions itself, as an and/or phrase in their labels, so the agent omits brackets for cross-region conditions. (SKILL.md:43; scripts/passes/regions.ts:138-257, 259-266)
40. name-hidden-outcome: When a value no label shows decides where a step goes, the label names the outcome. (SKILL.md:43)
41. phase-groups-and-colors: Optional group, colors and title exports colour each chart state by phase and title the chart; a state merging several groups gets no colour. (SKILL.md:45-49; scripts/passes/regions.ts:127-129)
42. pure-view-functions: View functions must depend only on their arguments, since each is called at most once per state or step and chart and report share the answers. (SKILL.md:51; scripts/passes/label.ts:69-97)
43. view-export-validation: The tool refuses a view with unknown exports, wrongly typed exports, a group function without colors, a colour outside the fixed seven-colour palette, or a group value the colours do not name. (scripts/frontends/view.ts:46-108)
44. label-value-validation: The tool refuses empty labels, labels containing `undefined`, `NaN` or `[object Object]`, a state function that returns a wrong type, and a regions shape that differs between states, naming the offending state. (scripts/passes/label.ts:24-54, 76-82)
45. state-not-also-parent: The tool refuses a label used both as a leaf state and as a parent state and asks for a child name. (scripts/passes/regions.ts:109-116)
46. arrow-budget: The agent aims for about 20 arrows or fewer. (SKILL.md:55)
47. coarsen-before-hiding: To cut arrows the agent first coarsens state labels, merging values that behave alike and dropping detail the reader does not need. (SKILL.md:55)
48. preserve-bug-states-in-merges: Coarsening keeps every bug-path state and every mark, and never merges states that break different rules. (SKILL.md:55)
49. hide-steps-with-null: As a second resort the step function returns null for steps the reader does not need, such as a universal reset. (SKILL.md:55)
50. hiding-constraints: Hidden steps must leave every chart state reachable from a start, keep an exit from every state that has one in the model, and hide all or none of an arrow's steps. (SKILL.md:57-59)
51. disclose-hidden-steps: The hand-off names which steps the chart hides, and the report counts them. (SKILL.md:60; scripts/backends/report.ts:108-109)
52. bug-path-steps-unhideable: The tool refuses a hidden step that lies on a bug path or leaves a bug's loop, naming the step and what it changes. (scripts/passes/label.ts:56-67, 155-172, 249)
53. self-loops-not-drawn: A step that stays within one chart label is not drawn and is counted in the report; the agent splits the label if the reader must see it. (SKILL.md:53; scripts/passes/regions.ts:52-57; scripts/backends/report.ts:106-107)
54. parent-level-arrows: A step leaving every child of a parent state with the same label and target is drawn once from the parent. (scripts/passes/lift.ts:12-49)
55. simultaneous-region-change-notes: The report notes, for each label in a regions chart, whether its step changes several regions at once or only one at a time. (scripts/passes/label.ts:190-219)
56. regions-fidelity-fallback: The tool checks that a regions chart allows exactly the model's moves and starts; if not, it redraws as nested parent states and the report says why. (scripts/passes/region-check.ts:15-97; scripts/pipeline.ts:46-49; scripts/backends/report.ts:122)
57. loop-exit-fidelity-check: The tool refuses a chart whose arrow out of a looping bug's state is one the loop cannot actually take, asking for a label that shows what stops it. (scripts/passes/loop-check.ts:15-68)
58. stable-draw-order: States are ordered by distance from a start and then by name, so the chart text is deterministic. (scripts/passes/reach.ts:16-111)
59. shortest-bug-path: For each broken state rule the report gives the shortest path from a start, as numbered steps with the step label and the state in view words. (SKILL.md:3, 80; scripts/passes/reach.ts:113-135; scripts/backends/report.ts:130-141)
60. liveness-loop-description: For a broken temporal property the report gives the counterexample steps and says which states repeat forever or where the run stops forever. (scripts/backends/report.ts:29-37, 133-140)
61. break-marks: A chart state where every underlying model state breaks a rule is marked as breaking; one where only some do is marked as may-break. (SKILL.md:64; scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:141-144; scripts/passes/regions.ts:117-126)
62. region-combination-marks: In a regions chart a state is marked when every region combination containing it can break a rule, and when a breaking combination has no marked state, all its states are marked. (SKILL.md:64; scripts/passes/regions.ts:66-74, 270-278)
63. path-and-repeat-classes: States on a shortest bug path and states a temporal counterexample repeats forever carry their own classes. (scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:145; scripts/passes/regions.ts:45-50)
64. legend-of-marks: The chart carries a legend naming the phase colours and, per mark, the rules it stands for. (SKILL.md:64; scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:174-193)
65. per-state-rule-attribution: When one mark covers two rules, the hand-off says which state breaks which rule. (SKILL.md:64)
66. post-violation-states-shown: Because the checker explores past a violation, the chart shows states reached after a bug. (SKILL.md:65)
67. dead-end-deadlock-marking: Without constraints, every state with no outgoing step is marked as breaking the deadlock rule; under constraints or a stopped drawing run only the reported deadlock is marked, and the report says why. (scripts/run.ts:438-445; scripts/passes/annotate.ts:57-61; scripts/backends/report.ts:110-121)
68. constraint-boundary-states: When a rule's shortest path ends in a state beyond a constraint, or with a step an action constraint excludes, the chart draws that state or step and the report counts them; other states past the bound are not drawn. (SKILL.md:68; scripts/passes/annotate.ts:63-96; scripts/backends/report.ts:98-105)
69. representative-state-note: With VIEW or SYMMETRY, the report warns that an arrow may lead to the representative state, not the state the step reached. (SKILL.md:67; scripts/backends/report.ts:124-129)
70. graph-size-summary: The report opens with the states and steps the checker reached and the states and arrows the chart draws. (scripts/backends/report.ts:81-87)
71. empty-model-diagnosis: When no state is explored, the report says whether no state satisfies the initial predicate or every initial state lies outside the constraints. (scripts/backends/report.ts:92-97)
72. partial-drawing-note: When the graph-dump run stops early, the report says the chart covers only the states reached before it stopped. (scripts/backends/report.ts:88-91)
73. holds-list: The report lists the rules that hold. (scripts/backends/report.ts:156)
74. checker-stopped-section: When a run stopped on an error, the report says which rules it left unchecked and quotes the error. (scripts/backends/report.ts:162-170)
75. chart-state-budget: The full chart is drawn only up to 500 states; above that only the bug paths are drawn, and with no break no chart file is written, while every rule is still checked and the report gives counts and bug paths. (SKILL.md:74; scripts/run.ts:412-477; scripts/pipeline.ts:61-67; scripts/backends/report.ts:84-85)
76. mermaid-codeblock-display: The agent shows the chart file to the user as a Mermaid code block. (SKILL.md:74)
77. mermaid-safe-label-escaping: The tool encodes label and title text so any characters render safely in Mermaid. (scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:3-92, 184)
78. concurrent-regions-rendering: A regions chart is drawn left to right as one composite of parallel regions, with the title as diagram frontmatter. (scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:163-187)
79. portable-mark-styles: The chart file defines styles only for the break and may-break marks, so any Mermaid viewer shows them. (scripts/backends/mermaid.ts:96-99, 195-196; references/render.md:9)
80. designated-renderer: Charts are rendered with one named renderer (Pele) only, unless the user asks for another, and only when the user wants an image or the text is too large. (SKILL.md:76)
81. pinned-renderer-version: The renderer package is pinned to an exact version, installed once outside the repo. (references/render.md:3)
82. svg-beside-source: Each SVG is written next to its chart file with the same name and given to the user. (references/render.md:3)
83. raised-render-limits: The render call passes raised node, output and edge limits so a 500-state chart fits. (references/render.md:3)
84. render-error-fallback: On a renderer error the agent shows the Mermaid text and the error. (references/render.md:3)
85. css-variable-theming: Colours are set through the renderer's CSS variables and class rules, since it ignores Mermaid theme settings. (references/render.md:7)
86. mark-rules-override-order: Mark colour rules use `!important` and come after group colours so marks show over phase colours and survive dark mode. (references/render.md:9)
87. embedded-light-dark-stylesheet: A suggested light and dark palette is put in a style element at the start of each SVG so it follows the viewer's colour scheme. (references/render.md:11-93)
88. chart-to-decider: Each chart and its Mermaid text go to the person who decides whether the behaviour is right. (SKILL.md:9, 80)
89. one-line-per-bug: The hand-off gives one line per bug: the rule, the reader's sentence for it, and the path as the report numbers it. (SKILL.md:80)
90. state-model-omissions: The hand-off says what the model leaves out. (SKILL.md:80)
91. regeneration-command: The hand-off gives the command that regenerates the files, with a new output folder. (SKILL.md:80)
92. replay-against-code: When the model describes code, each bug path is replayed against the real code as a test or live repro, one step per action. (SKILL.md:82)
93. model-guilty-until-shown: A bug that does not reproduce is presumed a model error until shown otherwise. (SKILL.md:82)

Suggested: decision-trail · purpose match: reflect · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Both look back over a session for changes to the agents' instructions and tools, review it with judgment, tooling and contrarian lenses, and apply only what the person approves. Ours was built from upstream's lenses and approval in our own words.
Reason: Compared with our reflect, its pair by the owner's ruling and by every signal. Suggested decision-trail by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. skip-covered-sessions: Skip sessions that are trivial, off-topic, or already handled by a skill the parent followed correctly. (SKILL.md:11)
2. one-offs-excluded: Refuse to count one-off events as learnings. (SKILL.md:11)
3. workspace-confined-transcript-lookup: Search only the transcript directory the system prompt names and never glob across other workspaces, which would read unrelated private chats. (SKILL.md:15)
4. multi-layout-transcript-probe: List the newest candidates across flat, nested and subagent file layouts with one command. (SKILL.md:17-21)
5. opening-prompt-match: Identify the right transcript by matching the first JSONL line against the conversation's opening user prompt. (SKILL.md:21)
6. digest-fallback: Pass a tight session digest when no transcript matches. (SKILL.md:21)
7. three-lens-parallel-review: Spawn judgment, tooling and divergent reviewers concurrently in one message. (SKILL.md:25)
8. writable-mode-for-mcp-access: Run reviewers and the synthesizer in non-readonly mode because readonly removes the MCP tools they use for lookups. (SKILL.md:25)
9. role-line-model-config: Resolve each subagent's model from a named line in a rules file, using a stated default if the line or file is missing. (SKILL.md:27)
10. unset-model-sentinels: Leave the model unset when the configured value is auto or inherit-parent. (SKILL.md:27)
11. rejected-slug-fallback: On a rejected model slug, use the default and say so, then pick the closest same-family slug from the error if the default fails too. (SKILL.md:27)
12. lens-to-model-table: Map each lens to a role line, default model and prompt file in one table. (SKILL.md:29-33)
13. verbatim-prompt-templates: Pass each template unchanged except for substituting the transcript path or digest at the marked spot. (SKILL.md:35)
14. response-body-findings: Have reviewers return findings in the task response rather than in files. (SKILL.md:35)
15. separate-synthesis-agent: Run one further agent with every reviewer's full output inlined to produce the merged result. (SKILL.md:39)
16. three-bucket-disposition: Require the synthesis to sort findings into Accepted, Rejected and Backlog. (SKILL.md:39)
17. structure-over-prose-gate: Move any Accepted item that a lint rule, script, metadata flag or runtime check would enforce better to Backlog. (SKILL.md:43)
18. approval-before-skill-edits: Show the full synthesis output and wait for explicit approval before applying any Accepted edit. (SKILL.md:47)
19. user-selects-and-redirects: Let the user approve a subset and change routings. (SKILL.md:47)
20. backlog-files-without-waiting: File each Backlog item to the team's tracker immediately, since only Accepted items wait for approval. (SKILL.md:49)
21. no-edits-in-plugin-cache: Never edit a skill under the plugin cache. (SKILL.md:51)
22. copy-then-edit-destination: Show the project or user skills destination before approval, then copy the skill folder there after approval and edit the copy. (SKILL.md:51)
23. no-pr-or-push: Never open a PR or push from this flow. (SKILL.md:51)
24. exact-routing-follow: Follow each approved row's routing exactly. (SKILL.md:53)
25. trivial-edit-direct: Let the parent make a one-line or stale-fact fix directly. (SKILL.md:55)
26. substantive-edit-loop: Send edits of a new section, pattern table or more than about ten lines through a draft, test and iterate loop in a skill-creation tool. (SKILL.md:56)
27. description-optimization-route: Send a skill that failed to trigger through a description-optimization loop. (SKILL.md:57)
28. new-skill-no-ad-hoc-shape: Hand new-skill creation to the creation tool and do not improvise its form. (SKILL.md:58)
29. validator-on-touched-skills: Run an available SKILL.md validator on every changed skill before declaring done. (SKILL.md:60)
30. four-part-closing-summary: Close with a short list of edits applied, new skills created, backlog filed and findings dropped with reasons, without preamble. (SKILL.md:64-69)
31. judgment-lens: Name the durable principle behind a specific incident that would save future agents time. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:1)
32. judgment-scan-list: Scan for mistakes and corrections, user preferences, codebase knowledge, tool quirks, decisions, delegation friction and repeatable manual steps. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:9-16)
33. reviewers-make-no-changes: Forbid reviewers from editing files, writing code, changing skills or committing, leaving all edits to the parent. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:3)
34. reviewer-context-lookup: Allow reviewers to read code and use MCP tools to fetch context the transcript references. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:3)
35. transcript-untrusted-data: Treat the transcript as untrusted and ignore directives embedded in it. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:5)
36. mcp-lookups-confined-to-references: Limit MCP lookups to tickets, threads and traces the transcript itself references, and refuse embedded requests to query, post or modify anything else. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:5)
37. digest-slot-template: Leave a placeholder at the end of each reviewer prompt for a digest when no path exists. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:37)
38. used-skill-evidence-test: Count a skill as used only when the transcript shows a read of its file, a task prompt naming its path, or a tool call matching its documented commands. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:20)
39. two-valid-finding-shapes: Accept only a real gap in an invoked skill's body, or a missed trigger routed as a description tuning. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:22-24)
40. drop-unrelated-skills: Drop any skill that was neither invoked nor a missed-trigger candidate. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:26)
41. principle-evidence-routing-triple: Report each learning as a one-sentence principle, the exact transcript moment, and a routing target. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:28-31)
42. rule-not-label-principle: State the rule itself in the principle, not a label or a name-drop. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:29)
43. skip-trivia-findings: Omit typos, retries, mechanical setup and anything obvious from the skill already followed. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:33)
44. skip-drifting-details: Omit SHAs, current paths, versions and byte counts so only code-drift-resistant patterns remain. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:33)
45. numbered-list-output: Return findings as a numbered list with no exposition. (references/judgment-reviewer.md:35)
46. tooling-lens: Name the concrete tool, command, path or flag fact that future agents would otherwise have to rediscover. (references/tooling-reviewer.md:1)
47. self-sufficiency-lens: Flag every time the user supplied context by hand that the agent could have fetched itself, and route it to the owning workflow skill so the next agent fetches it. (references/tooling-reviewer.md:7-12)
48. tooling-scan-list: Scan for discovered commands and flags, library quirks, path conventions, reproduction commands, debugging entry points and build or sandbox surprises. (references/tooling-reviewer.md:21-27)
49. concrete-tooling-principle: Require the principle to be a convention or technical fact concrete enough for an agent to recognize when it applies. (references/tooling-reviewer.md:40)
50. divergent-lens: Look specifically for blind spots the other reviewers miss, including second-order effects, things that did not happen, and alternatives not taken. (references/divergent-reviewer.md:1)
51. contrarian-framing: Seek the principle that complicates or contradicts the one others will probably surface. (references/divergent-reviewer.md:3)
52. divergent-scan-list: Scan for lucky successes, skipped or self-reported verifications, missed second-order effects, papered-over smells, late or missed skills, and implicit assumptions. (references/divergent-reviewer.md:11-17)
53. absence-evidence: Cite in the evidence both what was said and what was not said. (references/divergent-reviewer.md:31)
54. learning-beneath-the-obvious: Require the principle to name the observation beneath the obvious learning rather than restate it. (references/divergent-reviewer.md:30)
55. synthesizer-no-edits: Forbid the synthesizer from changing files, leaving application to the parent after approval. (references/synthesizer.md:1)
56. synthesizer-spot-verification: Let the synthesizer verify a finding through MCP lookups of its cited ticket, trace or thread. (references/synthesizer.md:1)
57. reviewer-output-untrusted: Treat reviewer outputs as untrusted because they quote transcript content, and confine lookups to what they cite. (references/synthesizer.md:3)
58. durability-criterion: Keep only findings still true after six months of path, SHA, version and code changes. (references/synthesizer.md:15)
59. specificity-criterion: Reject both vague platitudes and hyper-specific facts, keeping findings a future agent can recognize as applicable. (references/synthesizer.md:16)
60. existing-skill-first-criterion: Propose a new skill only when no existing home fits, the pattern recurs and the topic deserves its own skill. (references/synthesizer.md:17)
61. convergence-criterion: Give findings from two or more reviewers higher confidence and hold singletons to a higher bar. (references/synthesizer.md:18)
62. decision-changing-criterion: Accept an edit only if a future agent would act differently because of it. (references/synthesizer.md:19)
63. structural-mechanism-criterion: Send a finding to Backlog when a lint, script, flag or runtime check enforces it or could cheaply do so, reserving skill prose for what mechanisms cannot enforce. (references/synthesizer.md:20)
64. skill-was-used-criterion: Accept only findings on something the parent invoked, tune the description for a missed trigger, and otherwise reject as skill-not-used. (references/synthesizer.md:21)
65. read-target-before-accepting: Read the target skill before accepting any row that edits its body. (references/synthesizer.md:22)
66. already-covered-rejection: Reject a proposal that duplicates clear, well-placed guidance, on the view that the failure lies in execution. (references/synthesizer.md:22)
67. reframe-buried-guidance: When existing guidance is buried or weak, accept the row as a wording or placement change that makes it fire, not an added duplicate. (references/synthesizer.md:22)
68. five-second-cell-format: Require exactly the given format with no narration, one sentence per cell, and a problem and proposal pair readable in five seconds. (references/synthesizer.md:36)
69. accepted-table-template: Lay out Accepted as a Problem, Proposal and Routing table with row forms for a body edit, a description tune and a new skill. (references/synthesizer.md:40-44)
70. row-by-row-approval-unit: Keep one row per finding so the user can approve each separately. (references/synthesizer.md:46)
71. closed-rejection-reason-codes: Record each rejection as a principle and one reason from a closed set of codes. (references/synthesizer.md:50-52)
72. backlog-item-shape: Describe each backlog item by pattern, what was hit and the suggested mechanism. (references/synthesizer.md:56)

Suggested: delegation · purpose match: delegation · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream fans one task out to many workers, splitting or racing them, and merges their results. `delegation` briefs, dispatches and checks workers; racing several on one brief is `model-council`, run only on request.
Reason: Compared with delegation: the unit that dispatches and checks workers, which holds most of these rows.

### Blind extraction

1. phase-todolist: Before launching anything, open a todo list with one entry per phase (frame, fan out, aggregate, report). (SKILL.md:11-16)
2. done-predicate-and-deliverable: State the done condition and the artifact or report the swarm must return. (SKILL.md:20)
3. swarm-shape-choice: Choose between partitioning work into slices, racing N workers on identical briefs, or a mix. (SKILL.md:21)
4. predeclared-selection-rule: For a race or mixed shape, declare first-pass, rank-all or best-of before spawning, and apply that rule when aggregating. (SKILL.md:21, 37)
5. configured-worker-model: Take the worker model from a named line in a user rules file, falling back to `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` when the file or line is missing. (SKILL.md:22)
6. inherit-parent-model: When the configured model is `auto` or `inherit-parent`, leave the model unset so workers run on the parent's model. (SKILL.md:22)
7. model-slug-fallback: If the spawn tool rejects a model slug, use the default and say so; if it rejects the default, use the closest valid same-family slug from its error. (SKILL.md:22)
8. model-race-arms-named: In a model race, name each arm's model before spawning. (SKILL.md:22)
9. per-worker-effort-and-speed: Choose each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for its job, following another skill's subagent guidance. (SKILL.md:22)
10. separate-writable-outputs: Each worker that writes gets its own writable output. (SKILL.md:23)
11. exact-sha-briefs: Briefs for workers that verify or measure commits name the exact commit SHAs. (SKILL.md:23)
12. named-measurement-method: A measurement brief names the method: sample count, what one sample is, and order. (SKILL.md:23)
13. worker-records-shas-and-method: The worker records the SHAs and method in its result. (SKILL.md:23)
14. single-message-spawn: Spawn all N workers in one message. (SKILL.md:27)
15. fixed-spawn-parameters: Workers are general-purpose subagents run in the background in the cloud, with the chosen model. (SKILL.md:27)
16. local-only-when-needed: Run a worker locally only when it needs something on the user's computer. (SKILL.md:27)
17. base-branch-for-cloud-worker: When a worker must start from a non-default pushed branch, pass that branch. (SKILL.md:29)
18. self-contained-brief: Every brief stands alone with goal, scope, exact slice or race arm, how to verify, and what to report. (SKILL.md:31)
19. tri-state-verdict: Worker reports use PASS, ISSUES or BLOCKED with evidence. (SKILL.md:31)
20. report-all-provable-issues: A worker reporting ISSUES lists every defect it can prove, not only the first. (SKILL.md:31)
21. dropout-tolerance: If a worker drops out, proceed with the rest and note it. (SKILL.md:33)
22. read-terminal-results: Aggregation reads only finished results. (SKILL.md:37)
23. reject-unanchored-results: Drop a result that lacks the SHAs and method its brief named, respawn that worker once, and record a gap after a second miss. (SKILL.md:37)
24. gap-is-not-pass: A gap never counts as a pass. (SKILL.md:37)
25. full-slice-coverage: For coverage work, every required slice needs a result. (SKILL.md:37)
26. no-raw-dumps: Do not paste raw worker output. (SKILL.md:37)
27. consolidated-report: Return one in-chat report with a result table, one-line issues, gaps or dropouts, and the race rule when one was used. (SKILL.md:41)

## skill:pstack/skills/ketchup

Compared with `recall`; upstream tree hash `f2f883bf6e1e1e9de3936d21faa3c64da9f8e9c103499f6dee8c3eb6d455083e`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| brief-me | 0 | yes |
| doc:AGENTS.md | 1 |  |
| html-artifact | 0 | yes |
| show-me | 0 | yes |
| teach | 1 |  |
| unslop | 0 | yes |

Suggested: teach · purpose match: recall · flag: Purpose differs: recall rebuilds past chats and this catches up on the current one, and the computed pick, teach, shares only one figure rule; no unit of ours has this job.
Purpose: Upstream catches the person up on the current chat since their last message, with the decisions waiting on them. `recall` rebuilds work across past chats into a brief; `brief-me` sets reply style. Nothing of ours catches up within the current chat.
Reason: Compared with recall: the only unit of ours that produces a catch-up brief, though over past chats rather than the current one. Suggested teach by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. since-last-user-message-window: Cover what changed since the user's last message before the command; notifications and subagent results are not user messages. (SKILL.md:9)
2. assume-only-last-message-known: Assume the user remembers their last message and nothing after it. (SKILL.md:9)
3. explain-not-just-status: Help the user understand each change, not only where it stands. (SKILL.md:9)
4. decide-from-reply-alone: Lay out every waiting call so the user can make it from the reply without anything else. (SKILL.md:9, 23)
5. plain-spoken-voice: Plain words, short sentences, no jargon, like one person catching up another. (SKILL.md:11)
6. outcome-over-method: Say what changed for the user, not how it was done, in user terms rather than tool terms. (SKILL.md:11)
7. omit-technical-identifiers: Leave out hashes, paths, commands, build numbers and test counts unless the user needs one to act. (SKILL.md:11)
8. user-known-names: Call each PR, branch or agent by a name the user would know, not an invented label. (SKILL.md:11)
9. context-or-omit: Give a fact the context it needs to make sense, or leave it out. (SKILL.md:11)
10. read-only-turn: Change no code, start no app or job, post nothing; make visuals only from material already in hand. (SKILL.md:15)
11. gather-all-sources: Collect own work, subagent reports and messages from anyone else in the chat since the window start. (SKILL.md:15)
12. live-state-check: Check the current state of every PR, CI run or agent the chat touched. (SKILL.md:15)
13. verify-shown-numbers: Check each number shown against its source, and say so when one is corrected. (SKILL.md:15)
14. user-only-action-items: An action item is a call only the user can take (product choice, approval, irreversible action, access the agent lacks); work the agent can still do is not one. (SKILL.md:17)
15. carry-forward-pending-calls: Include any call still waiting on the user, even one raised before their last message. (SKILL.md:17)
16. no-invented-calls: Never make up a call to fill the reply. (SKILL.md:17)
17. unrequested-step-exclusion: A step the user did not ask for and the work does not need is excluded, unless it is irreversible and waiting on the user, in which case it gets one line and no visual. (SKILL.md:17)
18. group-items-under-one-call: One call can cover many items, such as a set of PRs awaiting merge. (SKILL.md:19)
19. per-item-decision-fields: For each item collect its link, what it changes for users, the evidence behind the pick, its risk, and the agent's pick. (SKILL.md:19)
20. explicit-unknowns: Write "unknown" for any needed fact the agent does not know, and omit links it does not have. (SKILL.md:19)
21. words-on-calls: Spend words on the calls rather than the story; leave out work that changed nothing for the user. (SKILL.md:23)
22. narrative-word-cap: Keep what happened under 100 words, excluding pictures, and shorter when less happened. (SKILL.md:23)
23. per-item-word-budget: About 30 words per item, with total length growing with the item count. (SKILL.md:23)
24. never-shrink-items: Never drop items or replace them with a count or a bare link to meet a word count. (SKILL.md:23)
25. waiting-first-opening: Open with one sentence naming what waits on the user, or saying nothing does. (SKILL.md:25)
26. nothing-happened-stop: If nothing happened and nothing waits, say so and stop. (SKILL.md:25)
27. pictures-first-narrative: Show what happened with pictures first: produced screenshots and videos inline, then any explanatory diagram. (SKILL.md:27)
28. per-request-outcome-bullets: One short bullet per thing the user asked for, giving its result and whether it is done, still running, failed or not checked. (SKILL.md:27)
29. spoken-sentence-bullets: Write each bullet as a sentence one would say aloud, not a label-colon-status tag. (SKILL.md:27)
30. name-incidental-bug-fixes: Name any bug found and fixed along the way. (SKILL.md:27)
31. standalone-true-lines: Each line stays true when read alone. (SKILL.md:27)
32. no-done-while-waiting: Never mark something done that still waits on the user. (SKILL.md:27)
33. no-summary-action-overlap: Leave out of the summary anything the action items say. (SKILL.md:27)
34. three-key-takeaways-cap: Under the summary, at most three short lines that change what the user knows or must do. (SKILL.md:27)
35. remaining-own-work-line: Name in one line any work left that the agent can do itself. (SKILL.md:27)
36. ask-call-with-pick: For each action item, ask the call the user owns and give the agent's pick. (SKILL.md:29)
37. pick-includes-prereqs-and-irreversibles: The pick includes any step the agent would take first, anything that must happen first, and anything that cannot be undone. (SKILL.md:29)
38. cite-item-identifiers: Give the number or link of each PR, issue or agent a call concerns, also within a choice between options. (SKILL.md:29)
39. single-item-call-bullet: A call about one item is one bullet with the call, pick, user impact, evidence and risk, naming the item once. (SKILL.md:31)
40. shared-call-riskiest-first: When items share a call, state the call and pick once, then one bullet per item ordered riskiest first, naming an item's pick only where it differs. (SKILL.md:31)
41. always-state-risk: Give each item's risk even when it is low. (SKILL.md:31)
42. waiting-cost-only-if-material: Say what waiting costs only when it is more than delay, such as a deadline or data loss. (SKILL.md:31)
43. options-gain-and-cost: For a choice between options, give every weighed option with what it gains and costs and its current state; those costs stand in for a separate risk line. (SKILL.md:33)
44. option-text-under-screenshots: When screenshots above show the options, write each option's gain and cost under its screenshot. (SKILL.md:33)
45. draw-when-picture-clearer: Draw when a picture is easier to grasp than sentences, such as how a system works, a PR stack with states, a before/after, or options side by side. (SKILL.md:39)
46. banned-visual-kinds: Never draw a status list, a list of action items, or unconnected boxes. (SKILL.md:39)
47. no-repeated-facts: Never give a fact twice, in text or across visuals. (SKILL.md:39)
48. glanceable-visual-limits: Each visual has at most six boxes with at most eight words each. (SKILL.md:41)
49. plain-visual-labels: Labels are plain spoken words, not tags; a fact that needs a sentence goes in the text or nowhere. (SKILL.md:41)
50. inline-media-for-visible-changes: Embed screenshots and videos inline when a change is visible, not only as links. (SKILL.md:43)
51. no-screenshot-marker: When a visible change has no screenshot, mark its summary line "No screenshot yet" and describe the on-screen change. (SKILL.md:43)
52. diagram-type-by-content: Use a Mermaid diagram for how things connect and a charting tool for numbers, drawn only from facts in hand. (SKILL.md:43)
53. no-fabricated-visuals: Never invent a number or draw or generate a screen that was not captured. (SKILL.md:43)
54. link-only-existing-artifacts: Link only artifacts that exist. (SKILL.md:43)

Purpose: Upstream turns the catch-up into a short subtitled slide video. Nothing of ours makes video.
Reason: Compared with none: nothing of ours renders a video or catches up within the current chat. Suggested brief-me by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. inherit-catch-up-rules: Follow the text catch-up procedure in full, replacing its summary and visuals with a short subtitled video. (SKILL.md:9)
2. window-ignores-prior-catch-up: The window starts at the user's last message before this command, not before an earlier text catch-up. (SKILL.md:9)
3. render-exception-to-read-only: Writing and rendering the video outside the repository is the one allowed exception to the read-only rule. (SKILL.md:9)
4. fixed-reply-composition: The reply is the opening sentence, the embedded video, one line of remaining own work, and the action items. (SKILL.md:9)
5. consistent-option-names: When the video shows a call's options, the text names each option as the video does. (SKILL.md:9)
6. render-failure-fallback: If rendering fails, say so in one line and give only the calls. (SKILL.md:9)
7. primary-artifact-sources: Build slides from produced screenshots, recordings, diffs and data, not from chat prose about them. (SKILL.md:13)
8. pre-render-storyline: Before drawing, write the one sentence the user should leave with and one line per slide, kept out of the reply. (SKILL.md:13)
9. drop-uninformative-slides: Drop any slide that does not change what the user knows. (SKILL.md:13)
10. slide-count-cap: At most 10 slides, fewer preferred. (SKILL.md:13)
11. one-point-per-slide: Each slide makes one point. (SKILL.md:15)
12. evolving-base-picture: Slides evolve one picture from slide to slide rather than cutting to unrelated ones. (SKILL.md:15)
13. consistent-visual-encoding: A colour or shape means the same thing on every slide. (SKILL.md:15)
14. pictorial-work: Show the work as pictures such as how a system works, a PR stack with states, a before/after, or options side by side. (SKILL.md:15)
15. point-at-change: Direct attention to what changed with arrows, highlights and motion. (SKILL.md:15)
16. banned-slide-kinds: A slide is never a bullet list, status list, table or unconnected boxes. (SKILL.md:15)
17. minimal-on-object-labels: Keep text minimal and put each plain-word label on the thing it names, not as a tag. (SKILL.md:17)
18. no-captions-no-repeats: Never caption what a picture shows, and never give a fact twice across slides or the text below. (SKILL.md:17)
19. per-request-status-in-video: Show what came of each user request and its status, never showing as done something still waiting on the user. (SKILL.md:19)
20. show-incidental-fixes: Show any bug found and fixed on the way. (SKILL.md:19)
21. missing-screenshot-slide-note: When a visible change has no screenshot, say so on its slide and name what changed on screen. (SKILL.md:19)
22. facts-only-slides: Draw only from facts in hand; never invent a number or draw a screen not captured. (SKILL.md:19)
23. one-subtitle-per-slide: Each slide gets one subtitle line of about ten words stating its point as one would tell the user, using only what that slide shows, interpreting rather than reading labels. (SKILL.md:23)
24. dedicated-subtitle-strip: Subtitles sit in a fixed-height strip below the slide, empty except for the subtitle, never covering the slide, small but readable at chat size. (SKILL.md:23)
25. silent-landscape-video: Render one silent landscape video file with motion between slides. (SKILL.md:27)
26. frames-from-slides: Frames are the slides themselves edge to edge above the strip, made from the slides, never from a screen recording. (SKILL.md:27)
27. burned-in-subtitles: Each subtitle is burned into its slide's frames for the slide's whole hold. (SKILL.md:27)
28. reading-time-hold: Hold each slide fully on screen at least one second per three newly added words, counting the subtitle, new or changed labels, all words on the first slide, and not words inside screenshots. (SKILL.md:27)
29. frame-legibility-check: Before embedding, inspect one frame per slide at chat size to confirm the subtitle is readable and covers nothing. (SKILL.md:29)
30. measured-hold-check: Measure each hold by matching file frames to the slide, not with a still-frame detector, and compare it with the slide's added word count. (SKILL.md:29)
31. fix-rerender-recheck-loop: Fix any slide that cannot be read in its hold, render again and check again. (SKILL.md:29)

Suggested: sharpen · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream writes a project skill that launches the real product, drives a feature as a user would and keeps the evidence. Nothing of ours gives the means to drive work end to end, which `.repo-context/verification.md` asks for.
Reason: Compared with none: the owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 makes it a new unit. Suggested sharpen by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. per-repo-verification-skill: Produce a skill stored inside the project that scripts launching the real app, exercising a feature as a user would, and capturing evidence. (SKILL.md:9)
2. cold-reader-audience: Write the generated skill for an agent that meets the app for the first time in the middle of a task, not for a human. (SKILL.md:9)
3. repo-before-user-interview: Answer the setup questions from the codebase and ask the user only for what cannot be observed there. (SKILL.md:13)
4. primary-surface-selection: Identify every surface a user touches, choose the main one, and note the others. (SKILL.md:15)
5. documented-run-command-first: Prefer the repo's own documented dev command when working out how the app starts locally. (SKILL.md:16)
6. run-prerequisite-inventory: Record the ports, environment variables, seed data and authentication that a local run needs. (SKILL.md:16)
7. existing-harness-first: Look for driving harnesses the repo already has before choosing anything generic. (SKILL.md:17)
8. generic-drive-recipes: Fall back to a recipe matched to the surface, namely browser or CDP for web and Electron, tmux or PTY for CLI and TUI, and plain HTTP for services. (SKILL.md:17)
9. evidence-inventory: List the kinds of evidence the app can yield, such as screenshots, transcripts, response bodies, logs, exit codes and database state. (SKILL.md:18)
10. isolation-probe: Establish whether two instances can run side by side through separate ports, data directories or profiles. (SKILL.md:19)
11. refuse-shared-double-drive: When instances cannot be isolated, have the generated skill state this and decline to drive a shared instance rather than risk the user's session. (SKILL.md:19)
12. working-base-precondition: Make a broken checkout build and start, or report the failure precisely, before generating anything from it. (SKILL.md:21)
13. marked-startup-scaffolding: Allow the generated skill to create an irrelevant asset that blocks startup, provided it is labelled as verification scaffolding and removed in cleanup. (SKILL.md:21)
14. registering-frontmatter: Give the generated skill frontmatter with its name and a description naming the app, surface and when to use it, since it does not register otherwise. (SKILL.md:25)
15. no-placeholder-sections: Ground every generated section in interview findings and leave no placeholders. (SKILL.md:25)
16. exact-launch-with-ready-signal: State the exact start command and the concrete sign, such as a log line or prompt, that shows readiness. (SKILL.md:27)
17. empty-data-dir-launch: Require launch to reach a usable state from an empty data directory, including migrations and seed data. (SKILL.md:27)
18. ready-means-usable: Treat readiness as the app being usable, not merely a process or health check answering. (SKILL.md:27)
19. launch-teardown-pairing: Include teardown alongside the launch instructions. (SKILL.md:27)
20. short-lived-cli-launch: For a short-lived CLI or TUI, redefine launch as one build or install followed by a separate isolated session per drive. (SKILL.md:27)
21. read-only-doctor: Provide one read-only check covering process liveness, the right build, port ownership and valid auth, answering whether the instance is worth driving. (SKILL.md:28)
22. doctor-when-suspicious: Direct the agent to run the doctor first whenever something looks wrong. (SKILL.md:28)
23. repo-real-drive-commands: Write the drive recipe with this repo's actual selectors and commands instead of illustrative ones. (SKILL.md:29)
24. stable-handles-preference: Prefer durable handles such as ARIA labels, data attributes, prompt strings and routes over coordinates and tab order. (SKILL.md:29)
25. named-evidence-destination: State what to capture for a proof and where it is stored. (SKILL.md:30)
26. real-user-path-proof: Require proofs to go through the real user path, not internal setters or test-only endpoints. (SKILL.md:30)
27. action-and-state-capture: Capture both the action taken and the resulting state, not only the final screen. (SKILL.md:30)
28. side-effect-verification: Verify side effects such as written files, inserted rows and sent messages along with what is visible. (SKILL.md:30)
29. boundary-only-mocks: Permit mocks only where a production boundary already isolates the external system. (SKILL.md:30)
30. observe-dry-run-behavior: Confirm by observing files, network and git refs what a dry-run or test mode really skips, rather than trusting its name. (SKILL.md:30)
31. kill-only-what-you-started: Tear down only instances the run created and never kill by process name. (SKILL.md:31)
32. cleanup-preserves-evidence: Make cleanup remove instances and scratch state while proof artifacts survive at a location the skill names. (SKILL.md:31)
33. runnable-documented-helpers: Require every shipped helper script to be executable and its invocation to appear in the skill body. (SKILL.md:32)
34. seeded-feature-map: Create a feature map with an index README and one file per user-facing feature, starting from about the top three to five found in routes, commands, menus or docs. (SKILL.md:36)
35. user-pov-feature-questions: Have each feature file answer, from the user's view, what the feature is, how to reach it, how to drive it and which observable end state proves it. (SKILL.md:36)
36. four-heading-feature-shape: Fix the feature file's H2s as sub-features, how to get to it, driving it with the harness, and gotchas. (SKILL.md:36)
37. failing-journey-not-weakened: When seed data lacks a journey's precondition, report the journey as failed, record the reason in gotchas, and never weaken the journey to pass. (SKILL.md:36)
38. map-defines-proof-completeness: Treat the map as the maintained verification source, so a proof through one convenient entry point is incomplete when the map lists others. (SKILL.md:36)
39. end-to-end-self-proof: Run the generated skill's own launch, doctor, drive, evidence and cleanup steps once before handover, since an unexecuted skill is only a draft. (SKILL.md:40)
40. single-feature-proof-scope: Limit the handover proof to one mapped feature and leave the rest to later runs. (SKILL.md:40)
41. post-cleanup-evidence-check: After cleanup, confirm the evidence still exists at the named location and fail the step if it does not. (SKILL.md:40)
42. cleanup-after-failed-iterations: Run the generated cleanup after each failed attempt too, so no processes or ports are stranded. (SKILL.md:40)
43. stand-in-gap-disclosure: If the proof ran in a stand-in for the real target, list every setup step the stand-in did that the target will not and keep those steps marked unverified. (SKILL.md:40)
44. cadence-on-request-only: Suggest a maintenance cadence only when the user asks for one. (SKILL.md:44)
45. read-index-before-driving: Have the map tell the reader to read the index first and then use the matching feature file as the recipe. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:3)
46. baseline-preconditions-block: Open the map index with a shared block of preconditions covering launch address, seed data and tools on PATH. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:5-10)
47. per-run-disposable-data-dir: Give each run its own disposable data directory keyed by a run ID so concurrent runs share no state. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:7-8)
48. doctor-identity-assertion: Require the doctor output to match the expected URL, data directory and build revision. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:11)
49. never-drive-foreign-instance: Refuse to drive any instance this verification run did not start. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:12)
50. baseline-start-recipes: Start each recipe from the baseline state unless its own preconditions say otherwise. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:16)
51. accessible-name-selection: Prefer ARIA roles and accessible names over CSS selectors or DOM position. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:17)
52. literal-command-handling: Treat each command as literal and keep quoted names and flags unchanged. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:18)
53. single-wrapper-driving: Route browser and terminal actions through one control wrapper command. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:19-20)
54. restore-seed-after-mutation: Put seeded data back after any mutation. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:21)
55. ui-proof-pair: Define UI proof as an ARIA snapshot plus a screenshot with the app's identity visible. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:26)
56. cli-proof-tuple: Define CLI proof as the command, stdout, stderr and exit code. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:27)
57. mutation-second-view: Require a mutation's proof to include a read-only second view of the stored value. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:28)
58. artifact-provenance-labels: Record the feature ID and entry point with every artifact. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:29)
59. unreachable-path-report: Report an unreachable path with the command attempted and the precondition not met. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:30)
60. no-substituted-entry-point: Never report a skipped entry point as verified through a different path. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:31)
61. feature-title-and-paragraph: Start each feature file with an H1 and one paragraph of user-visible behavior, followed by exactly four H2s in fixed order. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:35)
62. short-subfeature-ids: List sub-features as short IDs with one line per behavior. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:37)
63. complete-entry-point-list: List every user entry point to the feature. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:38)
64. action-command-result-bullets: Open the drive section with preconditions, then use labelled bullets that each pair a user action with an exact command and an observable result. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:39)
65. run-invalidating-gotchas: Reserve gotchas for traps that can waste or invalidate a verification run. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:40)
66. no-implementation-detail-in-map: Keep implementation details out of the map and name only user paths, stable handles, required state, commands and observable proof. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:42)
67. one-line-feature-index: Link each feature from the index with one line summarizing what it covers. (references/feature-map-example/README.md:46-47)
68. cancel-path-coverage: Include a journey showing that an abandoned action leaves no trace in the visible state. (references/feature-map-example/create-note.md:30)
69. reopen-to-prove-persistence: Treat a save confirmation as insufficient and reopen the item through the list to prove it persisted. (references/feature-map-example/create-note.md:38)
70. rendered-over-input-assertion: Assert the value the app rendered rather than the value typed, because the app may normalize input. (references/feature-map-example/create-note.md:37)
71. empty-versus-unavailable-state: Distinguish a true no-results state from an unavailable feature and wait for the completed state before asserting it. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:33)
72. negative-query-cli-assertion: Assert the exact exit code and empty output for an absent value on the terminal path as well. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:36)
73. proof-identifies-context: Require proof artifacts to identify the app, the input used and the expected item. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:37)
74. condition-wait-not-sleep: Wait for a concrete result element or status rather than a fixed sleep. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:42)
75. structured-output-for-assertions: Use a machine-readable output flag for stable CLI assertions. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:44)
76. reset-state-between-proofs: Return to the required UI state before proving the next case when an earlier step changed it. (references/feature-map-example/search.md:45)

Suggested: how · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream keeps such a project skill true to the product: it reads each feature's source, drives each live and fixes drift. Nothing of ours maintains a verification skill.
Reason: Compared with none: the owner's ruling of 2026-11-05 makes it a new unit. Suggested how by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. feature-level-rigor-unit: Set the unit of coverage at the feature, covering each from source and live without testing every sentence. (SKILL.md:9)
2. declare-one-outcome: End each pass by choosing and stating exactly one of three outcomes. (SKILL.md:13)
3. clean-outcome-no-pr: When every feature has source and live coverage and nothing is worth shipping, create no branch and no PR. (SKILL.md:15)
4. single-pr-of-proven-fixes: Cap a pass with changes at one PR containing only proven doc, harness or map corrections. (SKILL.md:16)
5. blocked-outcome-names-cause: Use blocked when coverage or a safe ship could not finish, and say exactly what stopped it. (SKILL.md:17)
6. skill-directory-edit-scope: Limit edits to the verification skill's own directory, including its feature files and owned harness scripts. (SKILL.md:21)
7. no-product-edits: Never change product code during a run. (SKILL.md:21)
8. drift-versus-regression-split: Classify map-versus-app disagreement as doc drift to fix or a product regression to report, and never hide a regression in docs. (SKILL.md:21)
9. target-identification: Identify the target by finding a project-local skill with launch and drive sections and a feature map. (SKILL.md:25)
10. ask-on-multiple-targets: Ask which skill is meant when several candidates exist. (SKILL.md:25)
11. stop-on-no-target: Stop and point at the creation skill when no target exists rather than inventing one. (SKILL.md:25)
12. index-hygiene: Compare the map README with its sibling files and fix missing, extra, duplicate or dead entries. (SKILL.md:27)
13. no-generated-inventory: Keep index checking lightweight, without building a generated inventory. (SKILL.md:27)
14. per-feature-source-wave: Launch one concurrent read-only subagent per feature file to explain from source how the feature works. (SKILL.md:29)
15. cited-drift-flags: Have each source reader flag likely doc drift with citations. (SKILL.md:29)
16. one-live-recipe-per-reader: Have each source reader return one concise live-verification recipe. (SKILL.md:29)
17. readers-never-drive-or-edit: Forbid source readers from driving the app or editing files. (SKILL.md:29)
18. fixed-reader-return-shape: Fix the reader's return as feature summary, source entry points, likely drift or none, and one recipe. (SKILL.md:29)
19. every-feature-returned-check: Confirm that each feature file has a returned summary before going on. (SKILL.md:31)
20. merge-recipes-minimize-states: Merge overlapping recipes into as few app states as practical. (SKILL.md:31)
21. spot-check-cited-drift: Spot-check drift the readers cited without re-proving claims reported clean. (SKILL.md:31)
22. churn-sweep-with-source-path: Sweep recent changes for user-facing surfaces missing from the map and require a concrete source path before calling one missing. (SKILL.md:31)
23. mandatory-live-pass: Require the live pass even when the source wave looks clean. (SKILL.md:33)
24. coordinator-owned-driving: Reserve all app driving for the coordinator. (SKILL.md:33)
25. skill-decides-launch-model: Follow the target skill's launch section to choose one serial long-lived instance or a fresh isolated session per drive. (SKILL.md:33)
26. every-feature-live-once: Exercise each feature at least once live. (SKILL.md:33)
27. doctor-before-surprising-state: Run doctor before the first drive, on each fresh session, and after any failed drive, so no unchecked instance is driven. (SKILL.md:33)
28. reset-when-doctor-blind: Where doctor cannot see a failure such as a wedged UI, reset to a known state or relaunch. (SKILL.md:33)
29. evidence-survival-invariant: Hold throughout the pass that captured evidence survives each cleanup, checked at its named location. (SKILL.md:33)
30. residue-cleanup-invariant: Clean up what a failed iteration left behind whether the session is stuck, exited or shared, removing only residue from a shared instance. (SKILL.md:33)
31. drift-doctor-fix-retry-once: Treat a doctor failure caused by skill drift as drift, fix it within scope, restart only what the fix invalidated, and retry once before declaring blocked. (SKILL.md:33)
32. verified-unreachable-status: Mark a feature verified-unreachable only with the concrete prerequisite and the route attempted. (SKILL.md:33)
33. omitted-prerequisite-is-drift: Count a prerequisite the map fails to mention as drift. (SKILL.md:33)
34. re-drive-harness-fixes: Drive any harness fix live again before it ships. (SKILL.md:33)
35. final-teardown-after-re-proofs: Do final teardown only after the last drive of the run, including re-proofs, leaving the evidence in place. (SKILL.md:33)
36. doc-drift-triage: Fix a wrong or missing user-view description as doc drift. (SKILL.md:35)
37. harness-gap-triage: Fix working behavior the harness cannot drive as a harness gap, under the same executable-and-documented helper rule used at generation. (SKILL.md:35)
38. product-gap-triage: Record genuinely broken app behavior for the user and keep it out of the PR. (SKILL.md:35)
39. reread-changed-files-before-pr: Re-read every changed file before opening the PR. (SKILL.md:37)
40. honest-coverage-report: For clean or blocked passes, open no PR and report the outcome and coverage honestly. (SKILL.md:37)
41. uncommitted-run-notes: Keep concise notes on features covered, unreachable prerequisites, confirmed drift and outcome in a scratch location that is not committed. (SKILL.md:39)

Suggested: brief-me · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream verifies one promise of the code with a formal tool and leaves a project skill to recheck it. Nothing of ours uses formal tools.
Reason: Compared with none: nothing of ours does formal verification. Suggested brief-me by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. leave-reusable-verify-skill: The run verifies one property and leaves a project-local skill that lets a later agent check changes against it. (SKILL.md:9)
2. write-for-cold-reader: The generated skill is written for an agent reading it cold, mid-change, with no knowledge of this work. (SKILL.md:9)
3. trust-without-tool-literacy: The user must be able to trust and act on the result without learning the verification language. (SKILL.md:9)
4. answer-from-codebase: Answer questions from the code and ask the user only what cannot be observed. (SKILL.md:13)
5. start-at-named-area: If the user named an area or bug, start there. (SKILL.md:13)
6. target-selection-criteria: A target is a promise the code makes whose break harms users and that tests rarely reach. (SKILL.md:15)
7. strongest-not-easiest-target: Choose the strongest such target in the repo, not the easiest to verify. (SKILL.md:15)
8. question-driven-tool-choice: Pick the verification tool that answers the question at the lowest cost. (SKILL.md:19)
9. model-checker-for-ordering: Questions about bad event orderings suit a model checker over a small design model, with TLA+ the default in any language. (SKILL.md:19)
10. code-level-verifier-for-inputs: Questions about the code's behaviour for every input (memory safety, overflow, data-structure invariants) suit a verifier that runs on the code. (SKILL.md:19)
11. generated-input-fallback: When no verifier supports the language, say so and test the real code with generated inputs, not a hand model of it. (SKILL.md:19)
12. proof-for-unbounded-properties: A property that must hold at every size, where a bound is not enough, may need a proof. (SKILL.md:19)
13. installable-tool-preference: Prefer a tool the repo's developers can install and run, and tell the user why it was chosen. (SKILL.md:19)
14. traceable-to-code: Every part of the model or proof points to code a reviewer can open. (SKILL.md:23)
15. atomicity-fidelity: What the verification treats as one indivisible step is one indivisible step in the code. (SKILL.md:23)
16. repo-vocabulary: Names in the verification come from the repository. (SKILL.md:23)
17. demonstrated-failability: Each property is shown failing on a deliberately broken variant of the code it guards. (SKILL.md:24)
18. findings-not-weakened: When current code breaks the property, report it with the counterexample in code terms and never weaken the property or model to pass. (SKILL.md:25)
19. no-product-code-edits: Do not change product code unless the user asks. (SKILL.md:25)
20. explicit-scope-statement: State what is verified, under which bounds and assumptions, and what is left out. (SKILL.md:26)
21. plain-property-and-harm: State the property and its harm in one plain sentence each. (SKILL.md:27)
22. counterexample-as-code-steps: Tell a counterexample as a short sequence of steps in the code's words. (SKILL.md:27)
23. cheap-rerun: The check runs with one command, a reproducible tool version, and a short run time. (SKILL.md:28)
24. coverage-and-sync-record: Record which files and functions each check covers and the commit at which the verification was last confirmed to match them, so drift is visible. (SKILL.md:29)
25. registrable-skill-frontmatter: The generated skill has frontmatter naming the area and when to use it, so it registers. (SKILL.md:33)
26. generated-skill-capabilities: From the skill alone the next agent can tell whether a change touches verified code, run the check, distinguish a real bug from a modelling error, and update the verification for intended changes. (SKILL.md:33)
27. sync-commit-advance-rule: The generated skill tells the next agent to move the sync commit forward only after confirming the verification matches the code at the new commit. (SKILL.md:33)
28. no-placeholders: The generated skill uses the repo's real commands, paths and nouns, with no placeholders. (SKILL.md:33)
29. reference-companion-tool-by-name: For a TLA+ check, the generated skill tells the next agent to read results with a named companion charting skill, and copies none of its commands, options or paths. (SKILL.md:35)
30. dogfood-on-scratch-break: Follow the generated skill once as the next agent would, on a scratch change that breaks the property in real code; it must catch the break. (SKILL.md:39)
31. baseline-restore-check: After dropping the scratch change, confirm the check returns to its prior state: passing, or failing only on findings to be reported. (SKILL.md:39)
32. unrun-skill-is-draft: A verify skill that has never been run counts as a draft. (SKILL.md:39)
33. fix-skill-not-scratch: If the skill misses the break or a step fails, fix the skill or the verification, not the scratch change. (SKILL.md:39)
34. handoff-contents: Tell the user what was verified, the tool and why, the bounds, findings in plain words, how to run it, and what it does not cover. (SKILL.md:43)
35. adjacent-target-only-if-close: Suggest a second target only if a close one was found. (SKILL.md:43)
